Title: MFA store Disabled - its own role-less customer passes with global on; a customer of another store naming it is asked for the code
Preconditions:
Fixtures are created IN THE CASE (FIFTH RULE) by scripts/seed-data/auth/mfa-fixtures.mjs: the account kind, the store and every flag come from the creator, never from a shared persona; the whole run is removed in Cleanup with teardown(runId). If the creator reports a fixtureGap for the kind this case needs, or the environment touched the state before the step that reads it, the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL.
Sign-in and change codes are read from the notification journal (MfaSignInEmailNotification for the account) with readLatestMfaCode({email, excludeIds}), where excludeIds = seen(account): the ids of every journal row already read for that account (the journal steps and the codes read earlier). A code is never selected by time ('after'): with its 10 s clock-skew window 'after' returns the PREVIOUS code while the new email has not arrived. SMTP is not relied on, and no code within 90s is BLOCKED.
SHARED-IMPACT WINDOW (global): the case sets MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled=true on {{BACK_URL}} and restores it in Cleanup. While it is on, EVERY store-less password sign-in on the stand needs a code (about 63% of the stand accounts have no confirmed email and cannot get one) - run it alone, never beside another sign-in suite, and keep the window short. The admin Bearer is minted BEFORE the window.
State under test: global on; the disposable store has StoreMode=Disabled; the own customer is a role-less confirmed-email customer of that store (kind customer-confirmed); the foreign customer is the same kind bound to the shared {{STORE_ID}}, which is a different store. Both name the Disabled store. VCST-6530: a Disabled store skips the code only for its own customers who are not Backoffice accounts; users of other stores follow the global setting. The code step comes before the store rule (suite 110 observed that the challenge precedes the store refusal), so the foreign customer's answer is the challenge, not user_cannot_login_in_store.
Steps:
[AUTH] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token (grant_type=password, username={{ADMIN_EMAIL}}, password={{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}) to obtain an admin Bearer token BEFORE any MFA setting is touched. Export it as VC_ADMIN_TOKEN so init() of mfa-fixtures.mjs reuses it instead of a password grant
[SETUP] import scripts/seed-data/auth/mfa-fixtures.mjs: init(); runId = a fresh 3-16 char [a-z0-9] string (it lands in emails, store ids and names)
[SETUP] store = createMfaStore(runId, {mode: 'Disabled'}) - an AGENT-TEST-MFA-<runId> store cloned from {{STORE_ID}} with an unresolvable .invalid URL (it can never capture the shared storefront); capture store.id and read StoreMode back ('Disabled')
[SETUP] own = createMfaAccount({runId: runId, store, kind: 'customer-confirmed'}) - an @example.com account with password {{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}} whose flags the creator verified; capture own.email, own.userId
[SETUP] foreign = createMfaAccount({runId: runId, store: {id: '{{STORE_ID}}'}, kind: 'customer-confirmed', n: 1}) - an @example.com account with password {{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}} whose flags the creator verified; capture foreign.email, foreign.userId
[SETUP] read GET {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings/MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled and remember the value as globalBefore; POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings with the admin Bearer and body [{"name":"MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled","valueType":"Boolean","value":true}]; GET it again and require true (the window is open from here)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/notifications/journal with the admin Bearer and JSON body {"notificationType":"MfaSignInEmailNotification","keyword":own.email,"sort":"createdDate:desc","take":20}; capture the number of rows as ownBefore and add the ids of those rows to seen(own)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/notifications/journal with the admin Bearer and JSON body {"notificationType":"MfaSignInEmailNotification","keyword":foreign.email,"sort":"createdDate:desc","take":20}; capture the number of rows as foreignBefore and add the ids of those rows to seen(foreign)
--- LAYER: Own customer, Disabled store, global on ---
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): grant_type=password, scope=offline_access, storeId=store.id, username=own.email, password={{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}}
[CAPTURE] resOwn = the response (status, error, errors[0].code, twoFactorToken, access_token presence)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/notifications/journal with the admin Bearer and JSON body {"notificationType":"MfaSignInEmailNotification","keyword":own.email,"sort":"createdDate:desc","take":20}; capture the number of rows as ownAfter and add the ids of those rows to seen(own)
--- LAYER: Customer of another store naming the same Disabled store ---
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/connect/token (application/x-www-form-urlencoded): grant_type=password, scope=offline_access, storeId=store.id, username=foreign.email, password={{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}}
[CAPTURE] resForeign = the response (status, error, errors[0].code, twoFactorToken, access_token presence)
[HTTP] POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/notifications/journal with the admin Bearer and JSON body {"notificationType":"MfaSignInEmailNotification","keyword":foreign.email,"sort":"createdDate:desc","take":20}; capture the number of rows as foreignAfter and add the ids of those rows to seen(foreign)
Assertions:
[STATUS] resOwn returns HTTP 200 with an access_token and no twoFactorToken: a Disabled store lets its own role-less customer in with the password alone while the global switch is on {SPEC} (VCST-6597 comment 112620: Disabled skips the code only for the store's own customers that are not Backoffice accounts) {DOC} (vc-module-mfa#3 README Configuration: StoreMode: Disabled: the code is not required from the store's own customers; Backoffice accounts and the users of other stores or without a store follow MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled there)
[COUNT] ownAfter equals ownBefore: no code email for the own customer {DOC} (vc-module-mfa#3 README: Delivery)
[STATUS] resForeign returns HTTP 400 with two_factor_required, a twoFactorToken and NO access_token: a user of another store follows the global setting (on) there, and the challenge comes before the store rule {SPEC} (VCST-6597 comment 112620: users of other stores follow the global setting) {DOC} (vc-module-mfa#3 README Configuration: StoreMode: Disabled: the code is not required from the store's own customers; Backoffice accounts and the users of other stores or without a store follow MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled there)
[COUNT] foreignAfter minus foreignBefore equals 1: the challenge sent exactly one code email {DOC} (vc-module-mfa#3 README: Delivery)
[BODY] resOwn and resForeign differ only by the store the account belongs to (same kind, same named store, same global state): the non-vacuity pair of this row {SPEC} (VCST-6597 comment 112620)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] the fixture creator (mfa-fixtures.mjs) reports no fixtureGap and no errors[] entry for the account kind and the store this case relies on
[API] response bodies are JSON with the documented error shape (error, code) and carry no stack trace
[NETWORK] no 5xx on /connect/token, /api/mfa/*, /graphql or the journal call
Failure_Signals: the foreign customer passes without a code (VCST-6530 not applied: the 3.1000.x behaviour where the named Disabled store decided for every user); the own customer is asked; the foreign customer answers user_cannot_login_in_store before any code (the global setting is not read first); no code email although two_factor_required; a 5xx
Cleanup:
FIRST, before anything else and even if the case aborted: POST {{BACK_URL}}/api/platform/settings with the admin Bearer minted before the window and body [{"name":"MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled","valueType":"Boolean","value":globalBefore}], then GET it and require globalBefore (a window left open blocks every other sign-in on the stand)
teardown(runId) of mfa-fixtures.mjs: removes every AGENT-TEST-MFA entity of the run (accounts, contacts, organizations, role, store) and asserts zero residue

Title: MFA own store Enabled - omitting the storeId, naming another store or an unknown one still asks the customer for the code (VCST-6495)
Preconditions:

Fixtures are created IN THE CASE (FIFTH RULE) by scripts/seed-data/auth/mfa-fixtures.mjs: the account kind, the store and every flag come from the creator, never from a shared persona; the whole run is removed in Cleanup with teardown(runId). If the creator reports a fixtureGap for the kind this case needs, or the environment touched the state before the step that reads it, the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL.
Sign-in and change codes are read from the notification journal (MfaSignInEmailNotification for the account) with readLatestMfaCode({email, excludeIds}), where excludeIds = seen(account): the ids of every journal row already read for that account (the journal steps and the codes read earlier). A code is never selected by time ('after'): with its 10 s clock-skew window 'after' returns the PREVIOUS code while the new email has not arrived. SMTP is not relied on, and no code within 90s is BLOCKED.
NO SHARED WINDOW: the case writes no shared setting. It uses only its own AGENT-TEST-MFA run store(s) and accounts; the global MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled setting is READ at the start and must be off (a global that is on decides the outcome for store-less requests, so the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL).
GraphQL documents (xAPI schema mfa; names, arguments and input types checked against .claude/knowledge/api/graphql-schema.md; a mutation takes its arguments in "command"): MFA_SETTINGS = query MfaSettings($storeId: String!, $organizationId: String) { mfaSettings(storeId: $storeId, organizationId: $organizationId) { storeId storeMode isRequired requiredBy userMode canChangeUserMode organizationId organizationMode canChangeOrganizationMode isProviderAvailable provider destination } } ; MFA_REQUEST = mutation RequestMfaChangeCode($command: InputRequestMfaChangeCodeType!) { requestMfaChangeCode(command: $command) { succeeded twoFactorToken provider destination resendSecondsRemaining lockoutSecondsRemaining errorCode errorDescription } } ; MFA_USER = mutation UpdateMfaUserMode($command: InputUpdateMfaUserModeType!) { updateMfaUserMode(command: $command) { succeeded errorCode errorDescription lockoutSecondsRemaining settings { storeMode isRequired requiredBy userMode canChangeUserMode isProviderAvailable } } }
State under test: global off; a disposable CustomerChoice store; org-mfa-member in a run organization; the member first turns its OWN mode On (so a stored value exists), then the administrator sets the ORGANIZATION to Required, then the member calls updateMfaUserMode with enabled=false and a valid code. The widget hides the switch (D30); the server's canChangeUserMode does not look at the organization (source), so what the API answers is recorded, not asserted (no spec); live (vcst 2026-11-04) the change succeeds and the stored mode becomes Off. The asserted invariant is the one the ticket states: the organization requirement comes first.

Assertions:
[DATA] sReq.isRequired is true and sReq.requiredBy is Organization: the company requires the code whatever the member's own mode {SPEC} (VCST-6597 description: The organization requirement comes first: a member can't turn it off with their own switch)
[DATA] sAfter.isRequired is still true and sAfter.requiredBy is still Organization after the member's attempt to turn the own mode off, whatever offTry answered {SPEC} (VCST-6597 description: a member can't turn it off with their own switch)
[STATUS] signIn returns HTTP 400 with two_factor_required and no access_token: the member's sign-in is still the second factor {SPEC} (VCST-6597 description: the organization requirement comes first)
[BODY] offTry.errorCode and storedUserMode.mode are recorded and NOT asserted (no spec): on vcst 2026-11-04 with a valid code updateMfaUserMode(enabled:false) succeeded and the stored user mode became Off, while requiredBy stayed Organization and the sign-in was still asked (the silent change the domain map calls D30, for the PO, not for the verdict) {OBSERVED} (vcst 2026-11-04) {DOC} (vc-module-mfa@1a0f481 MfaSelfService: CanChangeUserMode = isCustomerChoice && UserMode != Required, no organization look)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] the fixture creator (mfa-fixtures.mjs) reports no fixtureGap and no errors[] entry for the account kind and the store this case relies on
[API] every GraphQL response is HTTP 200 with data and/or errors[]; a refusal is a payload with succeeded=false and an errorCode, never a 5xx and never a stack trace
[NETWORK] no 5xx on /connect/token, /graphql, /api/mfa/* or the journal call
Failure_Signals: the member's change lifts the requirement (the sign-in becomes one step while the organization is Required); requiredBy changes to User; a 5xx
Cleanup:
before the teardown set every run account and organization whose mode the case changed back to Off with PUT {{BACK_URL}}/api/mfa/modes/{users|organizations}/{id} and the admin Bearer, so no non-default mode row is left behind

Title: MFA store Disabled - a Manager naming that store is asked for the code while global is on; the store's own role-less customer passes
Preconditions:
Fixtures are created IN THE CASE (FIFTH RULE) by scripts/seed-data/auth/mfa-fixtures.mjs: the account kind, the store and every flag come from the creator, never from a shared persona; the whole run is removed in Cleanup with teardown(runId). If the creator reports a fixtureGap for the kind this case needs, or the environment touched the state before the step that reads it, the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL.
Sign-in and change codes are read from the notification journal (MfaSignInEmailNotification for the account) with readLatestMfaCode({email, excludeIds}), where excludeIds = seen(account): the ids of every journal row already read for that account (the journal steps and the codes read earlier). A code is never selected by time ('after'): with its 10 s clock-skew window 'after' returns the PREVIOUS code while the new email has not arrived. SMTP is not relied on, and no code within 90s is BLOCKED.
SHARED-IMPACT WINDOW (global): the case sets MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled=true on {{BACK_URL}} and restores it in Cleanup. While it is on, EVERY store-less password sign-in on the stand needs a code (about 63% of the stand accounts have no confirmed email and cannot get one) - run it alone, never beside another sign-in suite, and keep the window short. Preconditions:

Title: MFA multi-organization contact - the contact's second (not current) organization is Required: the sign-in asks for the code, the requirement lifts when that organization is set back to Off, and what mfaSettings names for the current organization is recorded
Preconditions:
Fixtures are created IN THE CASE (FIFTH RULE) by scripts/seed-data/auth/mfa-fixtures.mjs: the account kind, the store and every flag come from the creator, never from a shared persona; the whole run is removed in Cleanup with teardown(runId). If the creator reports a fixtureGap for the kind this case needs, or the environment touched the state before the step that reads it, the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL.
Sign-in and change codes are read from the notification journal (MfaSignInEmailNotification for the account) with readLatestMfaCode({email, excludeIds}), where excludeIds = seen(account): the ids of every journal row already read for that account (the journal steps and the codes read earlier). A code is never selected by time ('after'): with its 10 s clock-skew window 'after' returns the PREVIOUS code while the new email has not arrived. SMTP is not relied on, and no code within 90s is BLOCKED.
NO SHARED WINDOW: the case writes no shared setting. It uses only its own AGENT-TEST-MFA run store(s) and accounts; the global MultiFactorAuthentication.Enabled setting is READ at the start and must be off (a global that is on decides the outcome for store-less requests, so the case is BLOCKED, never FAIL).
GraphQL documents (xAPI schema mfa; names, arguments and input types checked against .claude/knowledge/api/graphql-schema.md; a mutation takes its arguments in "command"): MFA_SETTINGS = query MfaSettings($storeId: String!, $organizationId: String) { mfaSettings(storeId: $storeId, organizationId: $organizationId) { storeId storeMode isRequired requiredBy userMode canChangeUserMode organizationId organizationMode canChangeOrganizationMode isProviderAvailable provider destination } }
State under test: global off; a disposable CustomerChoice store; ONE contact in TWO run organizations (kind b2b-two-org: orgs[0] is A, the current organization, orgs[1] is B). The creator binds this kind to {{STORE_ID}} unless the store argument carries b2bStoreId, so the case passes {id: store.id, b2bStoreId: store.id}: the contact belongs to the run store and the shared B2B-store is never touched; if the creator refuses it the case is BLOCKED (fixtureGap, a run-store twin of the kind is a request to the test-data-engineer), never FAIL. Every mode is Off at the start; the administrator then sets organization B (NOT the current one) to Required.
The oracle for the sign-in is BL-AUTH-021: a user needs the code when ANY organization of the contact requires it. What mfaSettings(storeId, organizationId = A) says is an open question and is phrased as one: {HYPOTHESIS} (VC-AUTH-004; no source says what the settings of the current organization report when another organization of the contact requires the code). Not observed live: the Test Model row 22 was a fixture gap on the discovery run.
Test_Data: back={{BACK_URL}}, store={{STORE_ID}}, admin={{ADMIN_EMAIL}}, admin_password={{ADMIN_PASSWORD}}, password={{DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD}}, graphql={{BACK_URL}}/graphql
Assertions:
[STATUS] signInA returns HTTP 400 with two_factor_required, a twoFactorToken and no access_token although the organization the request names (A, the current one) requires nothing {BL} (BL-AUTH-021: a user needs the code when any organization of the contact requires it) {SPEC} (vc-module-mfa#3 README: A user needs the code when their own mode or the mode of any of their contact's organizations requires it)
[STATUS] signInNoOrg returns HTTP 400 with two_factor_required: the requirement does not depend on which organization the request names {BL} (BL-AUTH-021)
[STATUS] signInOff returns HTTP 200 with an access_token and no twoFactorToken once organization B is back to Off: the requirement came from B and nothing else - the non-vacuity half of this row {SPEC} (VCST-6597 description: the organization requirement lifts when the organization is set back to Off)
[DATA] sA.isRequired is true and sA.requiredBy is Organization: the settings the storefront reads for the current organization name the company that asks for the code {HYPOTHESIS} (VC-AUTH-004: should mfaSettings report a requirement that comes from a non-current organization of the contact? not observed live; sA.organizationMode is recorded)
Cross_Layer_Checks:
[API] the fixture creator (mfa-fixtures.mjs) reports no fixtureGap and no errors[] entry for the account kind and the store this case relies on
[API] every GraphQL response is HTTP 200 with data and/or errors[]; a refusal is a payload with succeeded=false and an errorCode, never a 5xx and never a stack trace
[NETWORK] no 5xx on /connect/token, /graphql, /api/mfa/* or the journal call
Failure_Signals: the contact of a Required second organization is let in with the password alone; the requirement depends on which organization the request names; the requirement outlives the switch back to Off; mfaSettings says "not required" for a customer the sign-in asks (the rule enforced on one surface only); a 5xx
Cleanup:
before the teardown set every run account and organization whose mode the case changed back to Off with PUT {{BACK_URL}}/api/mfa/modes/{users|organizations}/{id} and the admin Bearer, so no non-default mode row is left behind
teardown(runId) of mfa-fixtures.mjs: removes every AGENT-TEST-MFA entity of the run (accounts, contacts, organizations, role, store) and asserts zero residue
